==Problem==
In the following list of numbers, the integer <imath>n</imath> appears <imath>n</imath> times in the list for <imath>1 \leq n \leq 200</imath>.<cmath>1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 4, \ldots, 200, 200, \ldots , 200</cmath>What is the median of the numbers in this list?

<imath>\textbf{(A)} ~100.5 \qquad\textbf{(B)} ~134 \qquad\textbf{(C)} ~142 \qquad\textbf{(D)} ~150.5 \qquad\textbf{(E)} ~167</imath>

==Solution 1==
There are <imath>1+2+..+199+200=\frac{(200)(201)}{2}=20100</imath> numbers in total. Let the median be <imath>k</imath>. We want to find the median <imath>k</imath> such that
<cmath> \frac{k(k+1)}{2}=20100/2,</cmath>
or
<cmath> k(k+1)=20100.</cmath>
Note that <imath>\sqrt{20100} \approx 142</imath>. Plugging this value in as <imath>k</imath> gives
<cmath>\frac{1}{2}(142)(143)=10153.</cmath>
<imath>10153-142<10050</imath>, so <imath>142</imath> is the <imath>152</imath>nd and <imath>153</imath>rd numbers, and hence, our desired answer. <imath>\fbox{(C) 142}</imath>.

Note that we can derive <imath>\sqrt{20100} \approx 142</imath> through the formula <cmath>\sqrt{n} = \sqrt{a+b} \approx \sqrt{a} + \frac{b}{2\sqrt{a} + 1},</cmath>
where <imath>a</imath> is a perfect square less than or equal to <imath>n</imath>. We set <imath>a</imath> to <imath>19600</imath>, so <imath>\sqrt{a} = 140</imath>, and <imath>b = 500</imath>. We then have <imath>n \approx 140 + \frac{500}{2(140)+1} \approx 142</imath>. ~approximation by ciceronii

Note by Fasolinka (use answer choices): Once you know that the answer is in the 140s range (200,000 is around 14^2 times 10^2) by the approximation, it is highly improbable for the answer to be anything but C.

==Solution 2==
The <imath>x</imath>th number of this sequence is <imath>\left\lceil\frac{-1\pm\sqrt{1+8x}}{2}\right\rceil</imath> via the quadratic formula. We can see that if we halve <imath>x</imath> we end up getting <imath>\left\lceil\frac{-1\pm\sqrt{1+4x}}{2}\right\rceil</imath>. This is approximately the number divided by <imath>\sqrt{2}</imath>. <imath>\frac{200}{\sqrt{2}} = 141.4</imath> and since <imath>142</imath> looks like the only number close to it, it is answer <imath>\boxed{(C) 142}</imath> ~Lopkiloinm

==Solution 3 (Answer Choices)==
We can look at answer choice <imath>\textbf{(C)}</imath>, which is <imath>142</imath> first. That means that the number of numbers from <imath>1</imath> to <imath>142</imath> is roughly the number of numbers from <imath>143</imath> to <imath>200</imath>.

The number of numbers from <imath>1</imath> to <imath>142</imath> is <imath>\frac{142(142+1)}{2}</imath> which is approximately <imath>10000.</imath> The number of numbers from <imath>143</imath> to <imath>200</imath> is <imath>\frac{200(200+1)}{2}-\frac{142(142+1)}{2}</imath> which is approximately <imath>10000</imath> as well. Therefore, we can be relatively sure the answer choice is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)} ~142}.</imath>

==Solution 4 (Geometry)==

We can arrange the numbers in the following pattern:
<cmath>\[
\begin{array}{cccccc}
\ &\ &\ &\ &\ 200 & \\
\ &\ &\ &\ 199 & \ 200 & \\
\ &\ &\ \iddots& \ \vdots& \ \vdots& \\
\ &\ 2& \ \cdots& \ 199& \ 200& \\
1 & \ 2 & \ \cdots& \ 199& \ 200&
\end{array}
\]</cmath>

We can see this as a isosceles right triangle, with legs of length <imath>200.</imath> 
<asy>draw((0,0)--(200,200)--(200,0)--cycle);
draw((142,0)--(142,142));
label("$x$",(142,0)--(142,142),E);
label("$x$",(0,0)--(142,0),S);
label("$200$",(200,0)--(200,200),E);
</asy>

Let <imath>x</imath> be the side length such that both sides of the triangle have the same area. The desired answer is then around <imath>x</imath> because about half of the numbers in the list fall on each side.

Solving for <imath>x</imath> yields:
<cmath>\begin{align*}
\frac{x^2}{2} =& \:\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{200^2}{2} \\
x^2 =& \:\frac{1}{2}\cdot 200^2 \\
x =& \:\frac{200}{\sqrt{2}} = \: 100\sqrt{2} \approx 141.
\end{align*}</cmath>
We see that <imath>\boxed{(C) \: 142}</imath> is the closest to <imath>x</imath> by far, and thus, can be relatively certain this is the answer.
